items.title: Sheila Jordan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I don‟t think I would ever have been heard had it not been for George Russell. ... George got that record date. ... he was very, very supportive.

ctx.x: Love For Sale. Okay? So then, during the, during the Monday night sessions, we‟d have different piano players and they were all good. So we had this one piano player, Jack Riley, who would play on Monday nights. So his teacher came down to hear him on a Monday night, and the teacher‟s name was George Russell. So he came down and he heard Jack, and he came over to me during the break. I had sung already. I had just sung. He said, “Where do you come from to sing like that?” I said, “Hell.” And we both started to…

the meantime, that was my very first, you know, professional recording. And then right after that, he paid to have a tape made―George Russell―of me singing songs that, all the songs that are on this Blue Note. That was George. George got that record date. He peddled this around to, to two different companies―Blue Note, who did not record singers, and uh, and Marcy, and the A&R man over there at the time was Quincy Jones. So Blue Note picked it up immediately and said, “Oh, we‟d like to record her.” And so George…

items.title: Sheila Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Middleburgh, New York, May 11, 2002
items.q: thanks to George Russell, who got me the Blue Note date

ctx.x: Was it a conscious thing at that time? I mean sometimes those things — I’ve heard stories about well this saxophone, this bass thing happened simply because the other people didn’t show up.

Oh no mine was like, mine was I loved the bass. And I remember thinking — actually my Blue Note album, I wanted it to be bass and voice but it was a little bit — nobody wanted to take that chance yet. But thanks to George Russell, who got me the Blue Note date, had made it a trio with guitar, Barry Galbraith, the wonderful Barry Galbraith, and so it was pretty similar but not quite. And there were a couple of things I did with bass and Denzil Best on drums. But originally I wanted that to be a bass and voice. But…
